messages:
maria: Heads-up: during the AWQ bakeoff on gpt-neox-20b we started seeing structured outputs drop from ~99.1% valid JSON to ~83% after quantizing to awq-4. 😬
kevin: wait — JSON validity or schema-level mismatches?
alina: concise — paste a failing example please
maria: JSON validity. function-calling args sometimes get truncated mid-object. reproducible on our eval set with deterministic seeds. small sample below:
```
PROMPT: call tool search for price lookup
EXPECTED: {"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "price of milk", "loc": "NY"}}
AWQ OUTPUT: {"tool": "search", "args": {"q": "price of milk", "loc":
```
kevin: ugh — truncation mid-object. Any pattern (numbers, punctuation, long strings)?
maria: mostly near numeric/short token boundaries (prices, years) and sometimes right after a closing brace. seems non-deterministic but high rate on AWQ.
prashant: what about GPTQ/int8 and fp8 runs? numbers?
maria: quick summary: GPTQ-int8: valid_json 98.9%
FP8 (fp8-symmetric): 95.6%
AWQ-4: 83.2%
(all on same evaluation set, same temperature=0)
eval-bot: Eval run registered: eval-2026-03-awq-schema-01 metrics: valid_json=0.832, arg_schema_match=0.88, tool_arg_edits=0.12
alina: could be quantization perturbing logits for separator tokens like '"', ':' or commas. can you dump token ids around the failure boundary?
maria: yes — sample token window (token:text:id):
```
'"': 34
'loc': 1234
':': 17
'NY': 876
'\"': 34  <-- repeated quote token appears slightly shifted in AWQ run
```
kevin: interesting — repeated quote token and shifted ids. hypothesis: grouped scale zeros or rounding cause softmax spike shift. did you try disabling kv-cache/prefix-cache?
maria: disabled KV cache — failure rate drops to ~77% (weirdly worse). with caching enabled it's 83.2.
prashant: maybe it's a compilation/kernel path difference used by AWQ vs GPTQ. AWQ uses per-group quant scaling; edge cases might zero small-group scales leading to margin errors on logits around punctuation.
alina: action items I'd suggest: 1) run logits-diff between fp16 and awq for the failing prompts 2) collect per-layer scale distributions for AWQ 3) reproduce with single-GPU deterministic run and enable full logprobs.
maria: already started #1 — small script below to log topk diffs and token probs: 
```python
# minimal repro to dump logprobs
resp_fp16 = client.generate(prompt, model='gpt-neox-20b-fp16', return_logprobs=True)
resp_awq  = client.generate(prompt, model='gpt-neox-20b-awq-4', return_logprobs=True)
# compare token-level argmax and top5 overlap around failure_idx
```
kevin: good. also try forcing greedy decode (no sampling) to isolate argmax diffs vs sampling noise.
maria: greedy reproduces mismatch too (so not sampling).
prashant: which infra? Hosted, Dedicated, or local? any sharding differences?
maria: failing on Dedicated (8xA100-80GB) during canary. small repro also on local docker with nvllm runtime.
alina: could be sharded matmul rounding differences across devices. check whether AWQ compiler uses mixed-precision tile kernels.
kevin: if this is customer-facing we should open a SEV. action: log the eval run, attach failing prompts, and mark canary paused if it hits threshold.
maria: ack — added failing prompts to the repro repo (internal link) and kicked off full logits-diff job. tagged @prashant @kevin on PR.
prashant: I'll take the deeper inference stack pass (quant scaling, kernel selection). will try re-quantizing with per-channel fallback for small groups.
maria: thanks — I'll keep the eval updated. current priority: block AWQ canary from rolling beyond test pool until we confirm root cause.
kevin: :thumbsup: great catch. if we confirm quant scaler issue we should add a corner-case unit test in the quantizer and a schema-based eval for structured outputs so future bakeoffs catch this earlier.
alina: agreed — adding structured-output-validity to CI evals is low-effort and high-value.
maria: noted. I'll open a follow-up ticket with failing examples, metrics, and the quick-repro script.
eval-bot: Incident flag suggestion: structured-output-regression detected on AWQ canary (rate > 5% above baseline).
prashant: thanks team — will update thread with findings and next steps.
kevin: ping me if you need extra GPU cycles or a mount to reproduce on a single-node exact-striping config.
